newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA NAPHTHA/MOGAS - GASOLINE TRADES LOWER.
newsitem.headline: ASIA NAPHTHA/MOGAS - GASOLINE TRADES LOWER.

text.p: The gasoline market on Thursday started to shrug off any bullish impact from firmer Western prices, amid low sales into the Philippines and the emergence of sellers in Singapore.
"The market is not very good..it's basically very well-supplied," said trader with an oil major.
Although the arbitrage to the U.S. West Coast is open, cargoes are difficult to move because of the strict quality requirements, he said.
"There is one window and so many people are trying to work it," he said.
Unleaded 92-octane was offered down from $23.30 per barrel and traded at $22.70 between Dutch and Japanese traders, traders said.
Unleaded 95-octane offers by a Swiss trader fell intraday to $23.10 from $23.50.
Reflecting the long market, sellers were also more aggressive into Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp's second import tender.
A South Korean refiner sold the 100,000-barrel cargo of 95-octane gasoline for early September at $3.20 per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes, on a cost-and-freight Bataan basis, traders said.
The seller was more aggressive in this tender than its last award for August at a less than $5 per barrel premium.

Sources said Petron was "sniffing around" for a mid-September cargo as its planned maintenance shutdown of a 85,000-bpd crude distillation unit No.2 and 17,000-bpd reformer may last longer than the scheduled September 1-12 timing, traders said.
Petron's buying was supportive but "no big shakes" for the long market, a trade said.
Naphtha remained under pressure with the absence of buyers.

Commenting on Wednesday's physical deal of 240,000 barrels of September naphtha at parity to Singapore quotes, fob, a trader said: "He (the seller) was lucky to find a buyer..I would be quite happy to move barrels at that price."
Naphtha August swaps were 30-40 cents per barrel lower at $21.70/$21.90, while gasoline was bid/offered at $23.50/$23.80 before the physical deal was done.
